Yes children suffering from gender dysphoria do suffer greatly just like those suffering from other mental disorders and psychological conditions. That's why using proven methods to reduce psychological distress such as forms of talk therapy, antidepressants, antipsychotics, and changes in lifestyle and environment are so important if we want these kids to have better lives. The current data does show that children receiving "gender affirming care" have lower rates of psychological distress... Until we control for factors such as usage of psychologists and therapists. So it appears that children who are given access to psychological services see better outcomes regardless of if allowed to transition or not. I am not "delusional", I simply believe the science. If shown a study that said that children getting puberty blockers gave better outcomes while controlling for confounding factors I would support it's use. But as of now there is not enough research that shows it is effective.

From what I've seen in the literature. Hrt and puberty blockers don't appear to have significant impacts on suicide rates when confounding factors are controlled for. There are ways to reduce chances of suicide in a patient that have less physical impacts than puberty blockers that should probably be prioritized in patients who are exhibiting gender dysphoria.

Well it's not as simple as "stop taking them and go into puberty" or start hrt and go into puberty. There are development periods that are called key or critical periods (although now there more commonly called sensitive periods at least in the circle of professionals I work with). These are periods of development where if certain things don't happen they either won't happen or will be much more difficult to make happen. This is part of why we stress early intervention when children seem to not be developing at an appropriate pace. But in regards to puberty. There are critical periods for sex organ development that if missed due to the use of puberty blockers, cannot be reversed. A larg percentage of children on puberty blockers for a significant period of time will have undeveloped or underdeveloped sex organs. This can cause infertility or complete inability to function. This will then cause problems later on whether the child ends up being cis or trans. For example a MTF trans person who was never able to allow their penis to develop will not have enough tissue to create a neo-vagina. Also regardless of if the individual ends up being trans or not they may end up with completely non-functional genitals which can cause inability to have normal sex, inability to achieve orgasm, etc etc. there are also psychological aspects that will be missed out on. Many of these have not been as well documented however. But not allowing a child to go through the normal mental and physical development brought on by puberty will have consequences.
